title: When matching junta examples are unavailable
statement: Let $P$ be a set of coordinates in the $n$-dimensional sign cube, let $z$ assign a sign to each coordinate in $P$, let $M$ be a natural number, and let a finite list of $R$ examples be given, each consisting of an input and an output sign. The procedure that selects $M$ examples whose inputs agree with $z$ on every coordinate in $P$ returns no selection if and only if fewer than $M$ examples in the list agree with $z$ on all those coordinates.
hypotheses_covered: $P$ is a finite subset of the $n$ coordinates
$z$ assigns a sign to each coordinate in $P$
The sample is a list of $R$ input-output pairs from the sign cube and the sign set
